_doc: Who a character hates, and what counts as one of them. Worth +10% damage in battle (see AbilityResolver). The match rules here were lifted out of Character.has_grudge_against, which used to carry them hardcoded.

_schema.display_name: Shown on the reveal and party screens.
_schema.blurb: One line. What was done, and to whom.
_schema.text: The authored history, a short paragraph.
_schema.matches: Any hit counts: factions[] | kinds[] | templates[] | template_contains[] (substring of the unit template id).

raiders.blurb: They came up the road once and took what could not be carried away again.
raiders.text: Not an army and not a cause — men with horses and a season to fill. What they leave is not a battlefield, it is a chore somebody else has to do.

imperial_usurpers.blurb: Copper stands the gate, white stands beside the throne, and neither ever names a reason.
imperial_usurpers.text: They came up the road one spring and did not explain. What they take, they administer, which is somehow worse than burning it.

the_dusk.blurb: Things that came through wearing shapes that almost work.
the_dusk.text: The Dusk does not raid, it arrives — and afterwards the village is still there and still answers, and something about it is wrong.

prowling_beasts.blurb: The wild does not hate anyone. It is simply hungry and closer than it was.
prowling_beasts.text: Beasts take the old, the slow and the ones who walked out alone, and they have been taking more of them every year since the gates opened.

goblins_and_vermin.blurb: Not a threat worth a song. Just the thing that never stops coming back.
goblins_and_vermin.text: Nobody writes down what goblins take, because it is a hen, a child's shoe, a stored winter. It adds up to the same thing in the end.
